data.title: Debt collection demand "last reminder before seizure" (likely scam)
data.summary: EuroClaim Forderungsmanagement Ltd. (Cyprus) demands €287.40 by 6 August 2026 for an alleged phone-concluded prize-draw subscription, threatening account seizure, a SCHUFA entry and criminal complaint. The letter shows several scam indicators.
data.explanation: This letter demands €287.40 within 72 hours to a Lithuanian IBAN held by a private individual, and threatens seizure, a SCHUFA entry and criminal charges. Real collection agencies do not usually ask for payment to a personal "trust account" abroad, and they cannot seize an account without a court order. The letter also says an objection is pointless, which is not true. Do not pay yet. Check whether you ever had this subscription, and ask for proof of the claim in writing (via the contact details you look up yourself). Consider contacting a consumer advice centre (Verbraucherzentrale) or the police. Keep the letter.

warnings: Payment is demanded within 72 hours to a Lithuanian IBAN held by a private person, a typical scam pattern.
The letter threatens seizure, SCHUFA entry and criminal charges without any court title, and claims an objection is pointless.
The letter gives no proper details of the alleged contract, uses a generic salutation and lists vague fees, so it may be a fake collection letter.
The stated deadline of 6 August 2026 has already passed as of today.
